facts.text: Hadera was founded on 24 January 1891 by Lithuanian and Latvian immigrants who purchased the land from Yehoshua Hankin, the “Redeemer of the Valley.”.
The city’s name comes from the Arabic word for “green,” reflecting the lush vegetation that once covered the coastal plain where Hadera now stands.
Hadera’s economy grew around a massive paper mill that supplies most of Israel’s paper needs, making it a key industrial hub.
The Orot Rabin Power Plant, Israel’s largest, sits on the Hadera Stream and its warm discharge attracts hundreds of sharks each winter.
A restored stretch of the Hadera Stream now serves as a park where visitors can watch sharks during the winter months from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. on weekends.
